'''D'ian''',<ref name="TEA" /> also known as '''Sen III''', was the third [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="Guide1" /> located in the [[D'ian system/Legends|D'ian system]], a part of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']] [[Corporate Sector/Legends|Corporate Sector]]. It was situated at the intersection of the [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlanes]] known as the [[Hydian Way/Legends|Hydian Way]], which linked it to the [[Bonadan system/Legends|Bonadan]] and [[Lythos system/Legends|Lythos systems]], and the [[Shaltin Tunnels/Legends|Shaltin Tunnels]], which connected to the [[Atchorb system/Legends|Atchorb]] and [[Etti system/Legends|Etti systems]].<ref name="TEA" />

D'ian was a balmy world featuring a mild climate and shallow [[Ocean/Legends|seas]], and it was known throughout the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] for its beautiful [[Flower/Legends|flowers]],<ref name="TEA" /> including the [[D'ian orchid vine]], which originated in the planet's [[D'ian province]]<ref name="Guide1" /> and was exported to the rest of the Corporate Sector. D'ian was also a successful [[Merchant/Legends|trading]] world that was home to several of the leading business schools of the [[Corporate Sector Authority/Legends|Corporate Sector Authority]].<ref name="TEA" />

==Behind the scenes==
D'ian was introduced as Sen III in the [[1984]] reference book ''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe]]'' by [[Raymond L. Velasco]].<ref name="Guide1" /> "[[Twinkle, Twinkle Little Star, How I Wonder Where We Are]]," a [[1990]] [[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game|roleplaying game]] source article published in the [[Voyages SF 13|thirteenth issue]] of the ''[[Voyages SF]]'' magazine, introduced the misspelled name "D'lan" for the planet and placed it in the [[Taldot sector/Legends|Taldot sector]]. Since that article was released outside of the [[Lucas Licensing]] process,<ref name="Twinkle">{{VoyagesCite|13|Twinkle, Twinkle Little Star, How I Wonder Where We Are}}</ref> it was considered non-[[canon]]ical with respect to the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity.<ref name="UnlicensedStatus">{{UnlicensedStatus}}</ref> The [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' by [[Daniel Wallace]] and [[Jason Fry]] subsequently identified the planet as D'ian and placed it in grid square S-3, also overriding the ''Voyages SF'' 13 placement by instead establishing it was part of the Corporate Sector.<ref name="TEA" />
